title: Keratolysis exfoliativa
summary: A common, harmless condition of recurrent superficial peeling on the palms and fingers, starting as air-filled blisters, usually in warm weather. Reassure, use emollients and avoid irritants.

glance.think: Recurrent ring-like peeling (collarettes) on the palms and fingertips, often in summer, with little itch or inflammation.
glance.engine: A defect in the cohesion of the outer stratum corneum; sweating and irritants make it worse.
glance.backbone: Reassure, emollients and urea or lactic acid creams, avoid soaps and solvents; steroids rarely help.
glance.never_miss: Pompholyx, hand eczema, tinea manuum and peeling after infection (scarlet fever, Kawasaki disease in children).

what: A common, **benign, non-inflammatory** disorder of recurrent superficial peeling of the **palms** (soles less often), mostly in young active adults. Synonyms: exfoliative keratolysis, **dyshidrosis lamellosa sicca**, (recurrent) focal palmar peeling, lamellar dyshidrosis. Often under-recognised and mislabelled as "hand eczema", which is why patients arrive having failed topical steroids.

list: Cause unknown; may run in families.

Splitting occurs **within the stratum corneum** — corneodesmosomes (the "rivets" between corneocytes) appear to break down prematurely, so sheets of horny layer detach (Chang et al., BJD 2012 described it as a distinct peeling entity; no causative gene identified).
**Aggravating factors:** heat/summer, **palmar hyperhidrosis**, and irritants — water, soap, detergents, solvents, friction. Roughly half of patients notice summer worsening.
Not an allergy, not infective, and not steroid-responsive inflammation.

head: Feature
Detail
rows: One or more tiny **air-filled** (not fluid-filled) superficial blisters on palms/fingers
Blisters burst → **expanding collarettes of scale** → round/oval peeled patches; multiple lamellae may peel
**Not itchy**; peeled areas can feel tender/dry and crack
Absent or minimal (no oedema, no vesicles with fluid, no lichenification)
Split can be deeper — skin feels **hard and numb** before it sheds (explains the numbness patients describe)
Heals to normal skin, then **recurs every few weeks**; chronic over years; often worse in summer

list: **Clinical** — history of recurrent non-itchy peeling + collarettes on non-inflamed palms.
Supportive tests if doubt: **skin scrapings negative** for fungus; **patch tests negative**; biopsy (rarely needed) shows cleavage within the stratum corneum.

**Pearl — the numbness:** usually explained by thick, deeply split fingertip horny layer; still ask about diabetes, B12/alcohol, carpal tunnel symptoms and vibration-tool use if numbness is persistent, sensory-distributed or present when skin is intact (diabetic neuropathy is a sensible safety-net).

head: Condition
Itch
Inflammation
Distinguishing clues
rows: Air-filled blisters → collarettes; recurs every few weeks; summer/sweat; steroid-unresponsive; no nail change; no smoking link
Erythema, dryness, fissures, glazed fingertips; wet work/irritant history; improves with avoidance + steroid
Deep-seated **fluid-filled** "tapioca" vesicles on finger sides/palms, then peeling
Sharp border, thick silvery scale, fissures, **nail pits/onycholysis**, plaques elsewhere, smoking link; usually worse in winter
Sterile yellow pustules → brown "rusty" dots; smoker; insteps/thenar eminences
Usually **one hand**, white scale in creases, check both feet/nails; scrapings positive

Keratolytic winter erythema (inherited, red peeling, winter), palmoplantar keratoderma, localised EB simplex (fluid blisters with friction), circumscribed palmar hypokeratosis, peeling skin syndrome (acral, genetic)

management: **Explain first:** benign, cosmetic-nuisance condition, recurrent, not contagious and not an allergy; tends to improve with age; steroids won't help (stop them — avoids palmar atrophy and wasted courses).

list: **Irritant avoidance:** cotton-lined waterproof gloves for wet work; soap substitutes; dry hands thoroughly.

**Emollient / keratolytic hand creams**, applied frequently: **urea** (e.g. 5–10% for maintenance, 10–25% for peeling — several UK OTC brands), **lactic acid** or **salicylic acid**-containing products; silicone/dimeticone barrier creams. US sources cite higher strengths (urea 20–40%, ammonium lactate 12%, salicylic acid 6%) — UK availability is limited, so use licensed UK products/specials per formulary.
**Treat hyperhidrosis** if present (topical aluminium chloride hexahydrate at night; refer for tap-water iontophoresis if severe) — reduces summer flares.

management: **Specialist options (refer if severe, painful fissuring, or diagnostic doubt):** acitretin (teratogenic, specialist-only, Pregnancy Prevention Programme), hand **PUVA**/photochemotherapy — limited evidence, reserved for refractory cases given skin-cancer and burden trade-offs.
red_flags: Peeling fingertips in a **child with fever** for 5 days or more: think Kawasaki disease (urgent).
Peeling after a sore throat and rash: scarlet fever.
pearls: "Peeling but not itchy, not red, worse in summer, steroid-proof" = think KE before re-issuing steroid.
Scrape any one-handed or treatment-resistant peeling to exclude tinea before labelling KE.
Avoid picking/peeling the lamellae — trim loose edges with clean scissors to reduce painful cracks.
Fingertip numbness that persists between episodes → examine/assess for neuropathy.
